source.author: lucr
source.text: omnis enim per se divom natura necessest immortali aevo summa cum pace fruatur semota ab nostris rebus seiunctaque longe; nam privata dolore omni, privata periclis, ipsa suis pollens opibus, nihil indiga nostri, nec bene promeritis capitur neque tangitur ira.
source.text_original: omnis enim per se divom natura necessest / immortali aevo summa cum pace fruatur / semota ab nostris rebus seiunctaque longe; / nam privata dolore omni, privata periclis, / ipsa suis pollens opibus, nihil indiga nostri, / nec bene promeritis capitur neque tangitur ira.
source.text_english: For all the nature of the gods must by itself enjoy everlasting life in utmost peace, far removed and utterly separated from our affairs; for, free from all pain, free from all dangers, strong through its own resources, needing nothing from us, it is neither won over by our good services nor touched by anger.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: Dissoluitur autem religio, si credamus Epicuro illa dicenti: omnis enim per se diuum natura necesse est immortali aeuo summa cum pace fruatur semota a nostris rebus seiunctaque longe., nam priuata dolore omni, priuata , ipsa suis pollens opibus, nil indiga nostri, nec bene promeritis capitur neque tangitur ira.
reuse.text_original: Dissoluitur autem religio, si credamus Epicuro illa dicenti: omnis enim per se diuum natura necesse est immortali aeuo summa cum pace fruatur semota a nostris rebus seiunctaque longe., nam priuata dolore omni, priuata , ipsa suis pollens opibus, nil indiga nostri, nec bene promeritis capitur neque tangitur ira.
reuse.text_english: But religion is destroyed if we believe Epicurus when he says these things: for the nature of the gods must of necessity, in itself, enjoy immortal existence in the greatest peace, removed and far separated from our affairs; for, free from all pain, free from care, strong in its own resources, needing nothing from us, it is neither won over by good deeds nor touched by anger.
